title: Operand Isolation
constraints: A datapath with an adder and a multiplier. Each unit has its own **operand registers** (`add_in = {add_a, add_b}`, `mul_in = {mul_a, mul_b}`), which are exposed as outputs.

On a rising edge with `en = 1`, only the selected unit's operand registers load `a` and `b`: the adder's when `op = 0`, the multiplier's when `op = 1`. The other unit's operands **hold**, so its logic doesn't toggle. The selected `op` is registered too.
`y` (combinational) = `add_a + add_b` if the registered op is 0, else `mul_a × mul_b` (16-bit). With `en = 0` nothing changes. Synchronous reset clears all registers.
hints: Without isolation, every operand change ripples through **both** the adder and the multiplier even though only one result is used. The multiplier is the expensive one.
Some designs AND the operands with the enable instead of holding them. Holding is better, since forcing zeros also toggles the unit.
